title: Slot arbitration protocol and cutover API contract for cross-team release trains
creator: Ava Kline
description:
Problem: multiple teams (runtime, console, api) need a deterministic way to reserve time/traffic slots for release cutovers and canary windows. Current ad-hoc calendar and Slack-based reservation process causes collisions, last-minute preemptions, and unclear fallback behavior which risks SLO breaches during launches.

Goal: define a lightweight slot arbitration protocol and a small, idempotent Cutover API contract that all product and infra teams can use to reserve, query, extend, preempt, and release launch slots. The contract must support: priority lanes, TTLs, soft vs hard reservations, preemption with grace windows, audit logs for compliance, observability hooks (metrics/events), and a rollback-safe fallback mode.

Scope: API spec (REST + idempotency keys), console UX hooks (slot list, cancel/extend flows), runtime integration points (preflight checks, graceful drain), acceptance tests and a migration plan for existing scheduled launches. Not in scope: global scheduling engine or long-term calendar marketplace (this ticket covers the protocol and contract only).

Trade-offs discussed: synchronous lock service vs optimistic reservation: we recommend a TTL-based optimistic reservation with a central arbitration layer for conflict checks to avoid blocking releases on a single leader. Preemption will be policy-driven (priority + approval path) rather than automatic to avoid noisy interruptions of critical launches. Auditability prioritized over minimal API surface to satisfy enterprise customers.
acceptance_criteria: API spec (OpenAPI) merged to repo: endpoints for POST /slots, GET /slots/{id}, PATCH /slots/{id}, POST /slots/{id}/preempt and DELETE /slots/{id}
Idempotency established: client-provided idempotency-key required for create and extend calls
Console UX mock and integration hooks documented and approved by design
Runtime preflight integration demo (canary pipeline) shows graceful drain using slot TTLs and preemption grace window
End-to-end integration tests covering create, extend, preempt, release, and automatic TTL expiry
Runbook drafted: owner rotation, escalation path, and rollback criteria for slot collisions
Telemetry: metrics and events shipped for reservation_attempts, reservation_conflicts, preemptions, and TTL_expiries
